full_judgment: 2. Briefly, stated the facts are that the plaintiffs petitioners instituted the aforesaid suit against the principal defendant opposite party No. 1 stating that the land described in the schedule of the plaint measuring .76 acres appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 2, S.A. Khatian No. 1, R.S. Khatian No. 1, C.S. and S.A. Plot No. 3352, and the R.S. Plot No. 824 of mows Berabari Thana, Mohanpur, District Rajshahi, was the khas property in possession of the ex-landlord. The plaintiffs predecessor Hayat Mollah took pattan of the disputed tank from the landlord in the year 1350 B.S. for the purpose of pisciculture and irrigation of agricultural land the plaintiffs predecessor  being in exclusive possession for mote than 12 years, acquired a rayoti right therein by paying rent to the Ex-landlord and thereafter to the government after the whole sale acquisition of rent receiving interest The plaintiff petitioners further stated that while enjoying as such by exclusive possession in their own right, title and interest. But at the commencement of S.A. operation in the preliminary stage in P.R.R. Khatian, the name of one Nader Mollah (brothers son Hayat Mollah) was also wrongly and jointly inserted with the name of the plaintiffs predecessor, Hayat Mollah though Nader Mollah had no right, title in the suit property. In order to avoid further litigation Hayat Mollah, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, purchased the portion Nader Mollahs share by a registered Kabala dated 7.9.64 vide deed No. 12844. It is further stated that for arrears of rent for the disputed property, a certificate case was started and Hayat Mollah the petitioners predecessor paid the arrear rent in the government Tashil office and got disputed tank free from all encumbrances and accordingly the name of the Hayat Molla was correctly recorded. But subsequently government official, on the plea of wrong entry in the S.A. record, refused to attest the name of the Hayat Mollah and thereby wrongly and illegally recorded the disputed tank in the khas khatian of the government. The plaintiffs are in exclusive possession of the same from the time of their predecessor Hayat Mollah and they have got right, title and interest in the disputed tank. The plaintiffs further stated that on 22.7.1984 the defendant No. 2 made an arrangement to lease out the disputed tank and against which the plaintiff No. 1 filed written objection but the defendant No. 2 without considering the same, rejected the objection and leased out the tank to the proforma defendant No. 4 Taser Mondal. The plaintiff asserted that in spite of the alleged lease, the said proforma defendant No. 4 got no possession and it is the plaintiffs who are still in exclusion possession of the said disputed tank. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the instant declaration suit.
